name: Bombo Palliative Care Project · cervical screening
status: Related initiative · AI not yet documented
geo: Bombo Regional Referral Hospital · Tanga, Tanzania
metricLabel: screening and treatment outcome totals in reviewed sources
short: Leah Norgrove and Ambrose Marsh supported integration of cervical screening with HIV and palliative care. AI use and quantified screening benefits are not documented in the reviewed sources. Newer data may be forthcoming.
outcome: Island Health’s 2018 report documents cervical screening for women living with HIV. A 2019 conference abstract describes integrated care at Bombo and reports that cervical cancer represented 48% of female cancers in the 2017 palliative-care data. This is a burden measure, not a screening success rate. Screening totals, treatment completion, mortality benefit and current screening activity were not verified.
partners: Bombo Palliative Care Project Society (Canada); Drs. Leah Norgrove and Ambrose Marsh; Dr. Violet Bakari and the Bombo HIV Care and Treatment Clinic team. The Society raises funds for local capacity and gaps in Tanzanian government support.
contact: Public correspondence email in the 2019 conference abstract. A direct project telephone was not verified. The abstract prints “Ambrose March”; Island Health confirms Marsh. Contact details have not been tested.
editNotes: Are there other centres of excellence used?
sampleDetails: Service report; no verified screening denominator.

name: ASPIRE Malongo · community HPV self-screening
metricLabel: women participated out of 1,496 invited
short: A 2025 Canadian conference report describes 99.7% participation, 318 of 413 HPV-positive women receiving VIA, and 291 receiving thermocoagulation. These are non-AI service outcomes.
outcome: CCRC 2025 abstract #2745 / poster #668: 1,492 of 1,496 invited women participated (99.7%). Of 413 HPV-positive women, 318 completed visual inspection (76.9%); 291 of those 318 received thermocoagulation (91.5%). Denominators differ: 91.5% is not the fraction of all HPV-positive women treated. Conference findings, not evidence of AI effectiveness or reduced mortality.
partners: ASPIRE partnership: University of British Columbia, Makerere University and Uganda Cancer Institute, with village health teams. Presented by Gina Ogilvie, BC Women’s Health Research Institute. A Malongo-specific financial sponsor is not identified in the cited abstract.
contact: Gina Ogilvie’s published scientific contact for the earlier ASPIRE Kisenyi trial (ISRCTN04500116). An ASPIRE research contact, not a verified Malongo clinic or current enrolment line. Email: Gina.ogilvie@bccdc.ca.
date: Conference findings November 2025 · program reviewed September 2026
sampleDetails: 1,496 invited; 1,492 participated; 413 HPV positive.

name: PRESCRIP-TEC / SAKHI AI decision support
metricLabel: AI field implementation evaluated
short: Women accepted the device with privacy safeguards; images supported remote review. Field performance lagged laboratory testing, and AI remained research-only.
outcome: September 2026 report: the mobile AI device was feasible but difficult to operate during clinic screening. Images supported remote second opinions and training. Field performance was poorer than laboratory performance; further tuning was needed. AI did not direct routine care. No treatment benefit is established by this implementation study.
partners: EU Horizon 2020, grant 964270. UMC Groningen, Uganda Cancer Institute, Manipal Academy, Friendship Bangladesh, icddr,b, URDT and Leiden UMC. The wider project ended in January 2024.
contact: Research contact published with Jaap Koot’s UMC Groningen affiliation. Not telephone-verified; not a patient booking line.
sampleDetails: Field implementation; AI did not direct routine care.

name: Cameroon 3T / Smart-Cervix
metricLabel: in six patient-perspective focus groups
short: A 2024 study found AI screening broadly acceptable with trusted clinicians and clear information. The larger Smart-Cervix diagnostic study is ongoing; its target is not a completed screening count.
outcome: The 2024 qualitative study involved 32 women in six focus groups in Dschang. It examined trust and acceptability, not diagnostic accuracy or treatment impact. HUG currently describes Smart-Cervix as a prospective AI video study with a 6,000-woman design; completed recruitment and final diagnostic outcomes were not verified.
partners: University Hospitals of Geneva (HUG), University of Geneva, EPFL and Dschang Regional Annex Hospital. Financial sponsor of the AI component is not specified in the reviewed institutional page.
contact: HUG gynaecology contact published on Prof. Patrick Petignat’s profile. Ask for the Cameroon / Smart-Cervix research team; not a direct trial-enrolment line.
date: Acceptability published 2024 · ongoing program reviewed September 2026
sampleDetails: 32 women in qualitative focus groups; separate 6,000-woman AI design is planned.

name: NCI / Global Good · Guanacaste AVE
metricLabel: AI discrimination of cervical precancer
short: AI achieved AUC 0.91 versus 0.69 for expert visual review and 0.71 for conventional cytology. Historical image validation, not a current AI screening service.
outcome: Published 2019: more than 60,000 images from a 1990s cohort of over 9,400 women, followed for up to 18 years. Retrospective AI evaluation achieved AUC 0.91, compared with 0.69 for expert image review and 0.71 for conventional cytology. AUC measures discrimination, not percent accuracy. Current AI deployment and treatment benefit are unverified.
partners: US National Cancer Institute (NIH) and Global Good, a fund at Intellectual Ventures; independent confirmation by National Library of Medicine experts. Included as foundational low-resource screening research.
contact: Published research-office number for senior investigator Mark Schiffman, NCI. Email: schiffmm@mail.nih.gov. Not a Costa Rica screening-service number.
sampleDetails: Over 60,000 archived images from over 9,400 women.

name: Dawa Health / DawaMom
geo: Company-listed: Lusaka, Zambia · Harare, Zimbabwe · Kigali, Rwanda
metricLabel: cervical-screening outcome figures on reviewed pages
short: AI screening, HPV self-testing and referral support are described. Cervical outcomes and city-level deployment are unverified; locations are company-listed.
outcome: Dawa describes computer-vision screening, HPV DNA self-test kits and follow-up guidance through community care. The reviewed pages give no cervical-screening counts, diagnostic accuracy or treatment-completion figures. Its research page lists maternal-health and anemia work, not cervical validation.
partners: Dawa Health and its clinician, community-worker and partner-clinic network. A cervical-program funder is not identified on the reviewed pages.
contact: Published primary contact. Alternative: +260 972 658 008. Email: hello@dawa-health.com. Not telephone-verified.
sampleDetails: Cervical-specific sample size not reported.

name: African AVE Collaborative
metricLabel: women enrolled across five countries
short: AI-assisted visual inspection detected 71.8% of significant precancers, versus 36.6% with visual inspection alone.
outcome: Published 2026. Of 24,447 participants, 39% were living with HIV. AI plus visual inspection achieved 71.8% sensitivity, with more false positives than visual inspection alone. HPV testing achieved 90.4% sensitivity. Outcomes are pooled across countries.
partners: Funded by Unitaid and Global Health Labs. Implemented by CHAI, ministries of health and clinical/research partners.
contact: CHAI headquarters. Ask for the cervical-cancer / AVE team; not a direct investigator line.
sampleDetails: 24,447 participants; pooled five-country results.

name: Hubei AI-assisted screening
metricLabel: screened in approximately six months
short: A later evaluation reported around 1.7 million screenings; about two-thirds of participants were rural.
outcome: 2017–2021: 1.52 million participants; 2,785 precancers and 191 invasive cancers detected. Only 64% of women requiring biopsy completed it. A 2024 evaluation reported around 1.7 million screenings in six months during 2022–23.
partners: Publicly financed through local authorities; Landing Med, local health centres, maternal-and-child hospitals and women’s federations.
contact: Landing Med company service number. Chinese 400 numbers may not connect internationally. Email: hello@landing-med.com.
sampleDetails: 1.52 million participants in the primary report; slides analysed by AI.

name: Kinondo Kwetu digital cytology
metricLabel: women living with HIV in the study
short: Approximately 96–100% sensitivity for abnormal cells against expert cytology. Routine AI service in 2026 is unverified.
outcome: Published 2021. Samples from 740 women were digitized locally. No expert-classified high-grade slides were classified negative by AI. Treatment for abnormal results was arranged and study-funded. Continued routine AI operation in 2026 was not verified.
partners: Kinondo Kwetu, University of Helsinki and Karolinska Institutet. Funders include the Erling-Persson Family Foundation, Swedish Research Council and Sigrid Jusélius Foundation.
contact: Hospital administration; ask for the digital-cytology research collaboration. Alternative: +254 732 364 747.
sampleDetails: 740 women with locally digitized cervical samples.

name: SAVECERVIX / EASTER · nGyn
metricLabel: sensitivity after multi-country retraining
short: Pooled retraining yielded 70% sensitivity and 81.1% specificity. Cross-setting performance remains a challenge.
outcome: May 2026 preliminary report: 1,820 women in India/Thailand and 1,200 Zimbabwean cases. Performance fell when transferred between settings. Retraining yielded 70% sensitivity and 81.1% specificity. Not yet established implementation success.
partners: IARC/WHO, NSV, University of Zimbabwe and participating Indian institutions. EASTER is funded by the US National Cancer Institute.
contact: NSV US technology-partner office, not trial enrolment. India office: +91 635 221 5152.
sampleDetails: Preliminary: 1,820 women in India/Thailand; 1,200 Zimbabwean cases.

name: CerviScanner / MednTech
metricLabel: women screened in the pilot
short: 84.5% agreement with expert clinical consensus across 251 complete records. Self-reported pilot results.
outcome: 2025 pilot: 260 women screened; 251 complete records. Reported 84.5% agreement with expert clinical consensus. Field sensitivity fell from controlled testing. Feasibility evidence, not proven treatment impact or clinical effectiveness.
partners: MednTech with Rwandan clinicians, frontline workers and research/public-health partners. Financial sponsor not identified. WHO contributed the report, which does not establish WHO funding.
contact: MednTech organizational directory listing. Ask for Maya Fakhfakh, Founder/Executive Director. Not independently telephone-verified.
sampleDetails: 260 screened; 251 complete records.

name: McGill–Paris multimodal cervical risk model
geo: Montréal and Paris · research institutions, not confirmed screening deployment
metricLabel: discrimination of CIN2+ in a referred cohort
short: Canadian–French collaboration combining clinical history and colposcopy. The estimated reduction in procedures has not been tested prospectively.
outcome: 2025 report: 6,356 conization/cone-biopsy cases after abnormal screening. Internal validation reported AUC 0.953 and accuracy 90.8%. At a 10% decision threshold, the authors estimated up to 35% fewer conizations without missing CIN2+ in their data. Assessment: encouraging diagnostic modelling, but a selected referral cohort, internal validation and a simulated treatment decision do not establish safe population screening or observed procedure reduction. Map locations denote author institutions; the reviewed abstract does not establish a Canadian clinical cohort.
partners: McGill University; École Polytechnique / Institut Polytechnique de Paris; Institute of the Cervix, Paris. Financial sponsor not verified in the accessible abstract.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: 6,356 conization cases; selected referral records.

name: NCI / CYTOREADER · automated dual-stain triage
geo: Northern California and Oklahoma · United States
metricLabel: colposcopy referral proportions under compared triage strategies
short: AI dual-stain reading preserved sensitivity and reduced the proportion referred to colposcopy compared with Pap cytology.
outcome: Online 2020, journal 2021: three study datasets contained 4,253 participants in total, including cervical and anal cohorts. Independent cervical validation at Kaiser Permanente found equivalent sensitivity and higher specificity than Pap and manual dual stain; referral proportions were 41.9% versus 60.1% for Pap. Assessment: strong comparative triage evidence, but these strategy comparisons are not a randomized demonstration of fewer cancers or deaths. The 4,253 total must not be presented as a cervical-only screening cohort.
partners: NCI Intramural Research Program / NIH / US Department of Health and Human Services; Kaiser Permanente; University of Oklahoma; Heidelberg collaborators.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: 4,253 participants across cervical AND anal datasets; automated dual-stain slides.

name: Genius digital cytology · Michigan validation
geo: University of Michigan · Ann Arbor, United States
metricLabel: mean slide-review time, digital versus manual
short: AI-assisted review was faster and more concordant with the original Pap diagnosis in a 319-case reader study.
outcome: 2024 study: nine readers assessed 319 selected Pap cases. Mean review time was 3.2 minutes digitally versus 5.9 manually. Agreement with the original diagnosis for exact Bethesda categories was 62.1% versus 55.8%. Assessment: useful workflow and reader-validation evidence. The reference was the original cytology diagnosis, not universal biopsy; selection enriched diagnostic categories. No population cancer detection or mortality benefit was measured. Kept separate from the German study because the cohorts and evaluations differ.
partners: University of Michigan; University of Pittsburgh; Hologic Scientific Affairs collaboration and system training. Financial sponsorship not independently established here; manufacturer involvement is disclosed.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: 319 selected Pap cases; nine readers.

name: Genius digital cytology · German co-screening validation
metricLabel: with histology available for 555 cases
short: German co-screening slides showed higher-grade abnormalities identified by digital review and shorter screening time.
outcome: 2023 report: 1,994 slides from routine 2020 co-screening were reassessed; 555 had histology. Exact cytology agreement was 86.56%, rising to 97.34% after follow-up/review. Digital review identified more ASC-H/HSIL and took less time. Assessment: supportive laboratory evidence, but retrospective, selected and partly adjudicated; the final agreement is not sensitivity for cancer. Industry funding and incomplete histology limit independent population-level conclusions. Not the same cohort as Michigan.
partners: CytoMol, Frankfurt; Frankfurt university clinic; Ulm University of Applied Sciences; BioTeSys. Funded by Hologic Deutschland GmbH.
contact: Direct project telephone and email not verified; use the linked publication to identify the corresponding research team.
sampleDetails: 1,994 slides; histology available for 555.

name: NHS AI cytology workforce model
status: Modelling study · not observed rollout outcomes · 2026
geo: England and Scotland · modelled laboratory workflows
metricLabel: modelled staff time per slide review/report
short: A UK workforce model estimated less staff time with AI-assisted cytology. These are projections, not measured service outcomes.
outcome: 2026 decision-tree study modelled 479,125 annual slides in England: 31,842 staff-hours with Genius versus 103,151 with manual microscopy; 4.0 versus 12.9 minutes per slide. Assessment: a roughly 69% reduction in modelled staff hours, not observed throughput, cost savings or cancer prevention. Estimates depend on published inputs and expert assumptions. Industry-supported modelling requires independent implementation validation; an existing service has not been verified by this report.
partners: NHS laboratory collaborators in England/Scotland; Aquarius Population Health. Funding: Hologic Diagnostics.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: Modelled 479,125 annual slides; not observed patient examinations.

name: DATEXIM / CytoProcessor · French laboratory studies
geo: French laboratory studies · Caen and Cherbourg collaboration
metricLabel: reported worker-time / diagnosis workflow comparisons
short: Two related French reports evaluated digital cytology against human/assisted slide reading; grouped as one technology program.
outcome: 2019 ThinPrep comparison selected 1,352 cases; a related Novaprep study selected 309. Reported workflow gains were 1.5× and 1.6× respectively. The ThinPrep report gave 1.5% versus 4% undercalled abnormalities against consensus cytology, with a denominator inconsistency (1,360 in results versus 1,352 selected). Assessment: promising workflow evidence, not histology-confirmed CIN2+ sensitivity or population false-negative rates. Manufacturer-led work and consensus adjudication warrant independent validation.
partners: DATEXIM and French clinical laboratories, including Centre Hospitalier Public du Cotentin. The Novaprep report lists European Regional Development Fund / EU support.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: 1,352 selected ThinPrep cases; separate 309-case Novaprep study.

name: Cerviray AI · Korean reader trial and Indonesian field report
status: Randomized reader study + small field comparison
geo: Two Korean centres; West Java, Indonesia · distinct study cohorts
metricLabel: Korean reader sensitivity with versus without AI
short: Strong Korean reader results did not translate directly into a small Indonesian VIA-comparison study.
outcome: Korea 2023: four readers assessed 886 images in a crossover study. Assisted sensitivity was 89.18% versus 71.33%; specificity 96.68% versus 92.16%. Indonesia 2025: 44 participants, with VIA as reference, gave AI sensitivity 42.9% and specificity 100%; expert image assessment was more sensitive (71.4%). Assessment: useful reader support but limited field transportability. The Indonesian result measures agreement with imperfect VIA, not biopsy-confirmed disease. Neither study establishes population mortality benefit.
partners: CHA University and Korea University; AIDOT technology; Indonesian clinical collaborators. Korean trial support: CHA University grant 2021-08-001; Indonesian sponsor not verified.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: 886 selected Korean images; separate 44-participant Indonesian study.

name: CerviCARE AI · Korean validation and Vietnamese community study
geo: Korea University Guro Hospital collaboration · South Korea; Vinh Long Province, Vietnam
metricLabel: reported sensitivity for the high-risk reference group
short: A selected 400-image validation reported high sensitivity, but the study used different reference tests for positive and negative cases.
outcome: 2024 report: 400 selected images, evenly split between reference-positive and reference-negative groups. Final validation reported 98.0% sensitivity for high-risk lesions and 95.5% specificity. Assessment: preliminary, enriched image-based evidence. Positives had histology whereas negative/atypical cases used cytology; this differential verification and careful image selection can overstate general screening performance. Earlier model-development figures in the paper differ from final validation; the headline refers only to final validation. Prospective external results are needed. Vietnam 2026: among 2,316 women with complete tests, agreement with VIA was 97.71% (kappa 0.918); AI flagged 360 versus 413 VIA-positive examinations. Without histological validation, this demonstrates concordance and feasibility, not diagnostic accuracy.
partners: Korea University Guro Hospital and collaborating investigators; NTL Healthcare imaging technology. Financial sponsor not verified from the reviewed source.
contact: Direct project telephone and email not verified; use the linked publication to identify the corresponding research team.
sampleDetails: Korea: 400 selected images. Vietnam: 2,757 women; 2,316 completed all three tests.
editNotes: 2026-09-20 review: Vietnam cohort added to the existing CerviCARE record, not duplicated. Publication year remains 2024 for the primary Korean report; additional report is 2026.

name: Sun Yat-sen / AICCS cytology validation
metricLabel: prospective cytology-classification performance
short: AICCS combined cell detection with slide classification and showed promising prospective accuracy.
outcome: 2024 study: 16,056 participants across development and evaluation datasets, not all prospective. The prospective assessment reported AUC 0.947, sensitivity 94.6% and specificity 89.0%; an assisted-reader experiment improved sensitivity. Assessment: substantial technical and reader evidence, but cytology grading is not the same as biopsy-confirmed cancer prevention. Generalisability beyond the tested laboratories and effects on treatment completion or mortality remain unproven.
partners: Sun Yat-sen University / Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital; Cells Vision and clinical collaborators. NSFC grant 82273204 and Guangzhou science-and-technology grants.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: 16,056 participants across development/evaluation datasets; slide-level assessment.

name: PUMCH / CAMS deep-learning cytology program
geo: Beijing, Shenzhen, Anhui and Zhejiang · China
metricLabel: reader sensitivity for cytological abnormalities
short: A 1,920-woman crossover reader trial improved sensitivity while preserving specificity. Related multicentre evidence is grouped here.
outcome: 2026 trial: four non-expert readers assessed slides from 1,920 women. AI assistance raised sensitivity to 85.7% from 71.3%; specificity was 86.5% versus 85.1%. Reading time fell from 175 seconds to about 30–31 seconds (abstract/body differ slightly). Reference: expert cytology consensus, not universal histology. A related 2025 program report found community-screening sensitivity similar to seniors but lower specificity (83.1% versus 90.1%). Assessment: good evidence for assisted reading, with a false-positive tradeoff in some settings; no established mortality benefit.
partners: Peking Union Medical College Hospital / Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and collaborating hospitals. 2026 support: CAMS Innovation Fund 2021-I2M-1-004; Shenzhen Sanming project SZSM202211032.
contact: Direct project telephone and email not verified; use the linked publication to identify the corresponding research team.
sampleDetails: Slides from 1,920 women; four non-expert readers.

name: Smart Scope CX · Indian primary-care validation
geo: New Delhi, Visakhapatnam, Cuttack and Chandigarh · separate Indian cohorts
metricLabel: histological verification among 871 screened in the main report
short: AI image assessment is feasible in primary care, but verification gaps and variable performance limit conclusions.
outcome: Main 2026 report: 871 screened, 69 underwent colposcopy and 40 biopsy; AI sensitivity 86.7%, specificity 92.0% and AUC 0.894 were calculated in the biopsied subset. A separate 268-woman Chandigarh study reported sensitivity 68.4%, specificity 65.5% and PPV 13.1%. Assessment: proof of concept, not reliable population accuracy; selective biopsy and loss to diagnostic follow-up create verification bias. Results vary across cohorts and must not be pooled or generalized as a single success rate.
partners: Safdarjung Hospital; KIMS-ICON; Acharya Harihar Post Graduate Institute of Cancer; separate Government Medical College Chandigarh study. Main report funded by NASSCOM Center of Excellence, India.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: 871 screened; 69 colposcopy; 40 biopsy.

name: South India nurse-led VIA-AI treatment triage
geo: Hyderabad-led nurse screening program · South India
metricLabel: reported clinical accuracy for cervical-feature assessment
short: VIA-AI explored support for nurse decisions on eligibility for ablative treatment.
outcome: 2024 pilot reported 76% clinical accuracy in comparative cervical-feature assessment and a 20% perceived false-positive challenge rate. The tool was tested within an ongoing nurse-led VIA program. Assessment: early feasibility and treatment-eligibility support; these measures are not biopsy-verified CIN2+ sensitivity or proof of reduced overtreatment. A controlled comparison of treatment appropriateness and follow-up is still needed.
partners: Public Health Foundation of India / Indian Institute of Public Health Hyderabad; Joly AI; Institute for Rural Health Studies. Conquer Cancer / ASCO International Innovation Grant (2021).
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: Pilot cervical-image comparison within nurse-led VIA service.

name: Hamamatsu GynAIe · cytology prioritisation
geo: Hamamatsu University School of Medicine · Japan
metricLabel: AI inference time per evaluable case, excluding preparation
short: AI ranked slides for human review. The short processing time is not the full diagnostic turnaround.
outcome: 2024 study tested 938 cervical specimens; 896 could be processed and 162 of 938 were classified inadequate overall. AI inference averaged 10.7 seconds per evaluable case, while scanning took 210 seconds and tile generation about 60 seconds per specimen. Assessment: promising prioritisation research, not a 10-second end-to-end screening service. Inadequate samples included high-grade abnormalities, and clinical confirmation remains necessary. Specimens can include repeat samples from the same patient; no measured cancer-prevention benefit.
partners: Hamamatsu University School of Medicine. Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research C, 20K07370, and HUSM Grant-in-Aid.
contact: Direct project telephone and email not verified; use the linked publication to identify the corresponding research team.
sampleDetails: 938 specimens, 896 processable; not necessarily 938 unique patients.

name: Wuhu AI-assisted cytology screening
metricLabel: women screened with human–AI review
short: Local implementation reported high agreement with manual review and increased reporting capacity; verification was selective.
outcome: 2024 report: 64,788 women, with 98.81% agreement between automated and manual reading. Reported daily output rose from 100 manual reports to a maximum of 1,000 remote reports. All AI-positive and a 10% sample of negative slides were manually reviewed. Assessment: useful implementation evidence, but agreement is not biopsy-confirmed cancer sensitivity, and peak output is not average throughput. Chinese and English abstracts reverse the 97.08%/98.94% sensitivity-specificity labels; these values are not used as definitive estimates. No long-term outcome benefit established.
partners: Wuhu Maternal and Child Health Hospital; Yangtze River Delta information-intelligence institute. Wuhu science/technology project 2022-cg16 and health research project 2023WUWJ2023y073.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: 64,788 women; AI cytology with partial manual verification.

name: CAIADS · Chinese colposcopy and biopsy guidance
metricLabel: junior-reader CIN2+ sensitivity with versus without AI in 2023
short: CAIADS improved junior-reader sensitivity in a selected referral cohort, while specificity remained low.
outcome: 2020 development used 19,435 patient records split for training, tuning and validation. A 2023 retrospective study included 366 of 1,146 clinic attendees with complete information and histology. Junior-reader CIN2+ sensitivity rose from 79.6% to 95.1% with AI; specificity was 48.3% assisted versus 48.7% unassisted. Assessment: promising assistance for biopsy evaluation, but substantial selection and low specificity limit general screening applicability. Reader assistance is not proof of better treatment or mortality outcomes.
partners: CAMS/PUMC and Chinese hospital/technology collaborators. Foundational study support included National Key Technology R&D 2018YFC1315504, CAMS, Shenzhen Sanming, Guangdong and Shenzhen programs.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: 19,435 retrospective patient records/images; later 366 complete clinic cases.

name: Georgia AI visual explanations · screening follow-up
metricLabel: reported follow-up adherence, AI visuals versus standard text
short: AI-generated illustrations plus simplified text improved reported adherence; this is communication support, not AI diagnosis.
outcome: Published online 2025: 3,000 women were randomized to standard text, enhanced plain text or AI-generated visuals plus text. Electronic-record follow-up adherence was 50%, 65% and 75%, respectively; comprehension was 65%, 78% and 90%. Assessment: encouraging pathway-level evidence, but the intervention combines visuals, simpler text and refinement with experts/patients. It does not isolate the benefit of generative AI over equivalent non-AI illustrations. Long-term outcomes and transfer to other cultures remain uncertain.
partners: Petre Shotadze Tbilisi Medical Academy and Charité Berlin collaborators. PubMed/Europe PMC lists German Federal Ministry of Education and Research support; award details not verified.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
sampleDetails: 3,000 randomized women; communication/adherence intervention, not an AI diagnostic test.

name: PAVE Consortium · HPV genotyping and AI visual triage
geo: Nine-country study, including four African sites
metricLabel: HPV-positive participants in interim analysis
short: Combines HPV genotyping with AI-assisted cervical image assessment in resource-limited settings.
outcome: Across nine clinical sites, HPV genotype and automated visual evaluation independently predicted biopsy-confirmed CIN3+ risk in 1,832 HPV-positive participants. Results support further implementation demonstrations; they do not establish reduced cancer incidence or mortality. This is the PAVE consortium study, distinct from the existing five-country African AVE record; the programmes share an AVE research lineage and their participant counts should not be pooled without checking overlap.
partners: PAVE consortium; NIH/NCI investigators and international clinical partners. Institutional involvement does not establish current funding at every site.
contact: No direct project telephone verified. Use the correspondence details in the linked publication.
sampleDetails: 1,832 HPV-positive participants; biopsy-confirmed CIN3+ risk.

name: CITOBOT AI · Colombian public-hospital screening
metricLabel: Sensitivity; specificity 94.9% in internal validation
short: AI colposcopy-image assessment evaluated among 650 women in a public hospital.
outcome: Study of 650 women (2023–2025) and 2,648 images used patient-level data partitions and biopsy reference. Internal validation reported 94.3% accuracy, 93.4% sensitivity, 94.9% specificity and AUC 0.98 for its binary screening endpoint. Independent multicentre and population validation is required before wider implementation; these are not demonstrated population health benefits.
partners: Pontificia Universidad Javeriana Cali; Red de Salud Ladera ESE; Alcaldía de Santiago de Cali.
contact: No direct project telephone verified. Use the correspondence details in the linked publication.
sourceLabel: CITOBOT study · Frontiers in Public Health (2026)
sampleDetails: 650 women; 2,648 images; patient-level partitions and biopsy reference.

name: Nodos Rosa · AI-assisted videocolposcopy
metricLabel: Diagnostic accuracy: AI-assisted versus conventional groups
short: Public-sector videocolposcopy evaluated against biopsy findings.
outcome: A retrospective comparison examined 782 records: 395 AI-assisted and 387 conventional examinations. Diagnostic accuracy was 80% versus 65%; sensitivity was 96% versus 93%. The groups were neither randomized nor paired, so these differences do not establish a causal benefit from AI.
partners: Tucumán Ministry of Public Health / SIPROSA; provincial cervical cancer prevention programme; Universidad Nacional de Tucumán.
contact: Published corresponding-author email (Italia Vega); no direct project telephone verified.
originalTitle: Inteligencia artificial: precisión diagnóstica de lesiones preneoplásicas de cérvix uterino
originalSummary: Comparación retrospectiva en el sistema público de Tucumán.
originalOutcome: Se revisaron 782 historias: 395 con IA y 387 convencionales. La precisión fue del 80% frente al 65%; la sensibilidad, del 96% frente al 93%. Sin aleatorización ni grupos pareados, no se demuestra causalidad.
sampleDetails: 782 examination records; 395 assisted and 387 conventional.

name: CYBO / JFCR · autonomous digital cervical cytology
metricLabel: Slide-level AUC for high-grade lesions or worse (HSIL+)
short: Whole-slide optical tomography and AI evaluated on 1,124 cervical cytology samples.
outcome: Four-centre evaluation of 1,124 samples reported slide-level AUC 0.86–0.91 for LSIL+ and 0.89–0.97 for HSIL+. The single-cell AUC above 0.99 is a different endpoint and should not be presented as patient-level accuracy. Multicentre validation does not establish population-level cancer prevention. The primary paper is English; a Japanese institutional announcement is available through the language toggle.
partners: CYBO; Cancer Institute Hospital of JFCR; University of Tsukuba; Juntendo University; Kaetsu health development centre.
contact: No direct project telephone verified. Use the correspondence details in the linked publication.
originalTitle: 世界初の臨床グレード自律型デジタル細胞診システムを開発
originalSummary: CYBOと共同研究機関による日本語の研究発表。原著論文は英語です。
originalOutcome: 4施設の1,124例で評価されました。AIを組み合わせたシステムは試験導入段階であり、集団検診でのがん死亡減少を示す結果ではありません。
sampleDetails: 1,124 samples across four centres; slide and cell endpoints differ.

name: Karolinska · machine-learning cervical screening risk models
metricLabel: Women in the temporal validation cohort
short: Machine learning predicts future high-grade cervical lesions from screening and demographic information.
outcome: Models were developed using 474,072 women invited in 2016 and validated using 370,105 invited in 2017. Validation AUCs ranged from 0.85 to 0.95 for the full-predictor model across prediction intervals. This retrospective risk-prediction study suggests potential for tailored screening; prospective implementation, transportability and improved clinical outcomes remain to be established.
partners: Karolinska Institutet. Reported funding: Vetenskapsrådet, FORTE, Karolinska Institutet, Horizon 2020 and Cancerfonden.
contact: No direct project telephone verified. Use the correspondence details in the linked publication.
sampleDetails: 474,072 women for development; 370,105 for validation.

name: THPS Afya Hatua / SEVIA · cervical cancer prevention
geo: Kigoma, Pwani, Shinyanga and Tanga, Tanzania
metricLabel: Women living with HIV screened across the programme
short: Integrated screening and treatment programme reporting smartphone imaging, remote expert review and AI support.
outcome: THPS reports 35,984 women screened, 929 precancer diagnoses, 898 treated (97% of those diagnosed), and 225 suspected cancers referred. Staff at 62 facilities received SEVIA training. These totals cover the wider programme, not an AI-only cohort. The implementer describes an AI component, but provides no independent AI sensitivity/specificity or comparative benefit estimate. This is a distinct implementing programme from Bombo; overlapping service populations should not be summed.
partners: Tanzania Health Promotion Support; PEPFAR/CDC-funded Afya Hatua Project; regional and council health teams, as reported by THPS.
contact: THPS institutional office; not a direct investigator line.
sampleDetails: 35,984 screened across wider programme; not an AI-only cohort.

name: TruScreen · Australian cervical precancer evaluation
geo: NSW: Sydney, Orange, Moree and Tottenham
metricLabel: Sensitivity / specificity for CIN2+ (high-grade precancer or worse)
short: Trained expert-system assessment of optical and electrical cervical tissue signals; Australian clinical evaluation.
outcome: Retrospective audit enrolled 506 women referred after abnormal cytology or HPV results; 474 had complete three-test comparisons. CIN2+ sensitivity/specificity: TruScreen 72%/71%, cytology 81%/95%, HPV testing 88%/76%. HPV testing was significantly more sensitive overall. TruScreen uses a trained pattern-matching expert system, rather than modern deep-learning image interpretation. Referral-clinic results do not establish effectiveness in general-population screening or reduced cancer mortality. Aboriginal services participated, but separate Indigenous performance estimates were not reported.
partners: Royal Hospital for Women; Orange Aboriginal Medical Service; Pius X Aboriginal Medical Service; Tottenham Multipurpose Hospital; UNSW; TruScreen investigators. No external funding reported; three authors disclosed company employment/advisory/consultancy relationships.
contact: Hospital gynaecological oncology enquiries; not a direct investigator line. Published corresponding author: Jessica Vet.
sourceLabel: Australian study · European Journal of Gynaecological Oncology (2022)
editNotes: Added following Australian evidence review. Original publication is English. Counts refer to the Australian cohort only; overseas studies of the same device are not counted as Australian deployments.
sampleDetails: 506 enrolled; 474 complete three-test comparisons.

name: MAVARIC · randomized automation-assisted cervical cytology
sampleDetails: 73,266 cervical samples; 48,578 paired readings.
metricLabel: Relative CIN2+ sensitivity versus manual reading
short: Historical randomized evaluation of ThinPrep Imaging and FocalPoint GS in Manchester.
outcome: Automation-assisted reading was less sensitive for CIN2+ than manual reading: relative sensitivity 0.92 (95% CI 0.89–0.95), with only a small specificity improvement. This negative trial matters when assessing automation claims, but does not determine the performance of every later AI system. No cancer-mortality benefit was established.
partners: University of Manchester; NIHR Health Technology Assessment programme.
contact: No direct telephone verified. Published contact details may have changed.

name: Finnish Papnet · randomized public-health screening
sampleDetails: 108,686 attendees: 72,461 conventional and 36,225 Papnet.
metricLabel: First-year lesion detection versus conventional reading
short: Neural-network-assisted cytology tested within Finland’s organized screening programme.
outcome: Histologically confirmed severe and moderate dysplasia detection did not differ significantly between groups. Specificity was 92.5% with Papnet and 92.9% conventionally. Routine feasibility was demonstrated; improved cancer prevention was not demonstrated by these first-year results.
partners: Helsinki University Central Hospital and Finnish organized screening investigators; specific funding not verified.

name: Ontario FocalPoint GS · two-laboratory validation
sampleDetails: 10,233 current and seeded abnormal slides.
metricLabel: Laboratory validation; not a patient screening count
short: Canadian evaluation before potential adoption of guided automated cytology.
outcome: No diagnostic-performance difference was found for LSIL+, HSIL+ or carcinoma compared with manual screening. False-negative rates for ASC-US and LSIL were higher with FocalPoint. Reference diagnoses were adjudicated cytology, not universal independent histology; abnormal-slide enrichment limits population inference.
partners: Mount Sinai Hospital, Toronto, and two Ontario laboratories; funding not verified.

name: BestCyte · Pinehurst cervical-slide reader validation
sampleDetails: 500 ThinPrep slides; three cytologists; enriched abnormalities.
metricLabel: ASC-US+ sensitivity against consensus cytology
short: Algorithmic cell sorting and galleries for primary cytology reading.
outcome: Reader sensitivity for ASC-US+ was 94.65–95.88%, versus 91.36% for the manual predicate. The reference incorporated reader concordance, creating incorporation-bias concerns; it was not a biopsy-defined screening endpoint. Selected slides and manufacturer-related interests limit generalization.
partners: CellSolutions; CellPathology Plus; Pinehurst/Marlboro Chesterfield laboratory collaborators.

name: Techcyte SureView · CorePlus digital cytology quality control
sampleDetails: 1,442 whole-slide images: 1,273 ThinPrep and 169 SurePath.
metricLabel: Sensitivity / specificity in laboratory validation
short: AI-assisted whole-slide quality-control workflow at CorePlus in Carolina, Puerto Rico.
outcome: Water-immersion scanning with AI achieved 82% sensitivity and 99% specificity against adjudicated cytology; reported accuracy was 97%. The laboratory adopted 100% quality-control review. This is a selected-slide workflow evaluation with industry involvement, not population CIN2+ accuracy or demonstrated mortality benefit.
partners: CorePlus; Techcyte; 3DHISTECH scanning platform.

name: UIS Bucaramanga · AI classification of cervical cell images
sampleDetails: 650 individual cell images; not 650 patient examinations.
metricLabel: InceptionV3 AUC for cell-image abnormalities
short: University-population cytology image evaluation, separate from CITOBOT’s clinical cohort.
outcome: InceptionV3 sensitivity/specificity were 93%/82%; MobileNet 78%/99%. These are cell-image results against expert interpretation, not patient-level CIN2+ detection. The restricted abnormalities and small local image sample require broader clinical validation.

name: CYTOVISION PAP · Russian comparative digital cytology
sampleDetails: 1,775 women provided samples; 773 slides selected for digitization.
metricLabel: Reported AI-assisted slide reading time
short: Russian study of automated preclassification in digital cervical cytology.
outcome: Abnormality detection was reported as 18% with digital AI-assisted cytology versus 10% conventional and 11% liquid-based cytology. Reading took 2–8 minutes, reportedly 2–6 times faster. Higher positivity is not proof of higher diagnostic accuracy: independent histological sensitivity and specificity were not established.

name: ECOSUR · low-cost automated cervical microscopy
sampleDetails: Nearly 2,000 cell-type images; patient count not established.
metricLabel: MobileNet test sensitivity / specificity
short: Robotized microscope prototype designed for resource-limited laboratories.
outcome: The reported test-set sensitivity was 97.95% and specificity 88.72% for classifying normal versus abnormal cell images. Production cost was below US$500 as estimated by the authors. Image-level validation does not establish whole-slide reliability, clinical screening accuracy or deployed service cost.

name: Laverty Pathology · Australian FocalPoint GS trial
sampleDetails: 2,198 routine split samples plus 38 seeded high-grade slides.
metricLabel: Unsatisfactory specimens: SurePath/FocalPoint versus conventional
short: Historical comparison of liquid-based guided screening and conventional Pap smears.
outcome: Unsatisfactory specimens fell to 0.2% from 4.1%. The nine histologically confirmed high-grade lesions in routine paired samples did not show a significant detection difference. Abnormal cells in the enriched high-grade set were located or triggered full review, but readers still missed some. Do not interpret system localization as 100% clinical sensitivity.

name: NAAMII / IISH · smartphone VIA screening research
sampleDetails: 1,430 women at 32 camps; only 25 biopsy results in the test subset.
metricLabel: Sensitivity / specificity in the small biopsy subset

name: Debre Markos · machine-learning cervical risk in HIV care
sampleDetails: Secondary records from four antiretroviral clinics; not a new screening trial.
metricLabel: Limited discrimination despite reported 98% accuracy
short: Exploratory risk classification among women living with HIV using routine clinical records.
outcome: The reported K-nearest-neighbours model had 98% accuracy but AUC 0.68. The large difference makes accuracy alone misleading. This retrospective, cross-sectional modelling study does not establish prospective screening benefit or reliable precancer triage; external validation is needed.

outcome: The local image evaluation reported 98.09% classification of normal cells and 80.49% of abnormal cells.
